body:
`person:group-yes-bank-rana-kapoor` · flag: **severe** · confidence: verified · tickers: YESBANK

Flag: SEVERE (Kapoor era); Yes Bank today is controlled by institutional holders (SBI-led rescue 2020; Japan's SMBC became the largest shareholder in 2025 -- stake size ~20-25%, verify). Kapoor built Yes Bank (2004) into a top-5 private lender via fast corporate lending to stressed groups (ADAG, Essel, DHFL, IL&FS, Cox & Kings, CG Power). Early signals: RBI asset-quality divergences (FY16-17 ~Rs 4,200 cr; FY17 ~Rs 6,355 cr); RBI refused Kapoor a further term (Sep-2018); promoter pledges on Yes Bank shares; founder-family dispute with the Madhu Kapur side; frequent auditor and board exits (2018-19). RBI imposed a moratorium (5-Mar-2020) and an SBI-led reconstruction; Rs 8,415 cr of AT1 bonds were written off (the Bombay HC quashed the write-off in Jan-2023; Supreme Court stayed that ruling -- litigation ongoing). SEBI fined Kapoor Rs 2 cr for mis-selling AT1 bonds to retail investors (2021). CBI/ED allege Yes Bank invested ~Rs 3,983 cr in DHFL debentures in 2018 in exchange for ~Rs 600 cr in kickbacks to Kapoor family firms (DoIT Urban Ventures); Kapoor was arrested in Mar-2020 and released on bail in all cases after four years (Apr-2024); trials pending; no final conviction found. Lesson: for banks, RBI divergence disclosures and regulator refusals of CEO tenure are the decisive early signals; minority equity in a rescued bank is massively diluted (rescue at Rs 10/share vs ~Rs 400 peak).

- **regulator findings:** RBI divergences; SEBI AT1 mis-selling penalty; RBI moratorium 2020
- **allegations:** CBI/ED DHFL kickback case (pending)

- **Lakonishok and Lee (RFS 2001):** insider purchases are informative, especially in small firms. Insider sales are not.
- **Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski (JF 2012):** trades by "opportunistic" insiders earn about 82 bp a month (value-weighted). Trades by "routine" insiders earn about 0.
- **13F filings:** they are lagged by up to 45 days and show long positions only. Use them for idea sourcing and crowding checks, not for cloning. The best-ideas and 13D-activism findings have not been verified yet.

body:
| Case | The good number | Why it misled | Test that catches it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Satyam's 'cash-rich, debt-free' balance sheet (`case_study:hidden-trap-satyam-cash`) | Rs 5,361 cr cash and bank (Sep 2008), steady growth, ~20%+ margins, NYSE listing, Big-4 audit | Rs 5,040 cr of the cash and Rs 376 cr of accrued interest were fictitious; fake FDs even attracted tax on fake interest | interest income / average cash vs FD rates; why hold huge cash AND borrow; why no buyback/dividend |
| Wirecard's fintech growth, margins and EUR 1.9 bn cash (`case_study:hidden-trap-wirecard-margins-cash`) | fast revenue/EBITDA growth, ~25-30% EBITDA margins [approx], DAX member, EY audit, EUR 1.9 bn cash | profits came from Asian 'third-party acquirers' it did not control; the cash 'in trustee accounts' did not exist | where do profits come from (segment you can audit?); cash held by trustees/escrow; CFO ex customer funds vs EBITDA |
| DHFL's 33% AUM growth and low reported NPAs (`case_study:hidden-trap-dhfl-growth`) | AUM ~Rs 1.1 lakh cr, +33% YoY in FY18; profits +25%; low gross NPAs; cheap vs HDFC | growth came from developer/project and wholesale loans (project loans +55% YoY), many to promoter-linked entities, funded by short-term CP/MF money | ALM gap in 1-year bucket; share of CP funding; wholesale/project loan growth vs retail; borrower concentration and promoter links |
| Yes Bank's 17.7% ROE and 1.28% gross NPA (`case_study:hidden-trap-yes-bank-roe`) | FY18 ROE 17.7%, RoA 1.6%, GNPA 1.28%, loan growth 54%, premium P/B | NPAs were under-recognised (RBI divergence Rs 4,177 cr FY16, Rs 6,355 cr FY17); growth came from corporate loans to stressed groups | RBI divergence disclosures; loan growth >30%/yr in corporate book; CASA ratio; exposure to stressed groups; regulator action on CEO |
| Manpasand's growth faster than Frooti (`case_study:hidden-trap-manpasand-growth`) | revenue +33-44% (FY18, ~Rs 955-985 cr), PAT +256% in Q4 FY18, growth outpacing market leader Parle Agro | sales were inflated through fake invoices to shell distributors (CGST: ~Rs 691 cr outward bogus transactions); receivables outgrew sales | growth vs category leader; receivables growth vs revenue; capex verification; distributor names; auditor exit |
| Vakrangee's 40% ROCE, zero debt and positive CFO (`case_study:hidden-trap-vakrangee-roce-debt-free`) | ROCE 37-43% (FY15-18), OPM 24-26%, debt cut to zero by FY18, PAT Rs 680 cr, CFO Rs 669 cr (FY17) > PAT | economics far above what a rural kiosk/e-governance franchise business can earn; sales jumped and margin halved in FY18 as low-margin trading was added; then revenue collapsed 77% | margin vs business physics and peers; revenue mix shifts; parabolic price; auditor resignation |
| Luckin's store and same-order growth (`case_study:hidden-trap-luckin-growth`) | explosive store count and revenue growth after a May-2019 IPO; improving store-level margins | COO fabricated ~RMB 2.2 bn of 2019 Q2-Q4 sales; items-per-order inflated | independent foot-traffic/receipt data; founder share pledges; capital raises right after IPO |
| Valeant's 'cash EPS' growth from acquisitions (`case_study:hidden-trap-valeant-eps-growth`) | rapid growth in adjusted 'cash EPS' and revenue; star investors; low R&D cost base | growth was bought with ~$30 bn of debt and price hikes; recurring acquisition costs were excluded from 'cash EPS'; an undisclosed pharmacy (Philidor) channelled sales | organic volume growth; GAAP vs non-GAAP gap; debt/EBITDA; price vs volume; related distribution channels |
| GE's smooth earnings, low P/E and dividend (`case_study:hidden-trap-ge-smooth-earnings`) | decades of steady EPS beats, 'reasonable' P/E, long dividend record, AAA-era reputation | smoothness came from GE Capital and accounting levers (receivable factoring, contract-asset 'deferred monetisation'); hidden long-term-care insurance liability | dividend vs FCF; contract assets vs revenue; receivables sold; earnings volatility too low for the businesses |
| Rajesh Exports at 9-20x P/E on Rs 2 lakh cr of revenue (`case_study:hidden-trap-rajesh-exports-low-pe`) | P/E 8-20 (median ~15), ROCE 17-20% (FY15-17), PAT ~Rs 1,000-1,300 cr, positive CFO most years, 'world's largest gold refiner' after Valcambi | 0.4-1% margins on huge pass-through gold revenue made profit unverifiable; SEBI's interim order (Jun 2026) alleged ~Rs 12,557 cr standalone revenue overstated FY21-24 and the forensic auditor was denied records | tiny margin x giant revenue = small errors swamp profit; segment/geography disclosure; auditor changes; access for forensic audit |
| PC Jeweller's growth, profits and low P/E (`case_study:hidden-trap-pc-jeweller-inventory`) | fast sales and profit growth, a 'cheap' P/E vs Titan, expanding store count, export business | inventory and export receivables (UAE) grew faster than sales; CFO weak or negative for years; profits were not turning into cash | inventory + receivable days trend; CFO/PAT; who the export customers are; promoter share 'gifts' |
| Ricoh India's MNC parent and revenue surge (`case_study:hidden-trap-ricoh-india-mnc-growth`) | Japanese parent with ~74% stake, Big-4 audit, revenue surge into 'managed document services', stock ~10x | out-of-books entries manufactured profit (Rs 66.7 cr in Q1 FY16 alone turned a loss into a profit); receivables and unbilled revenue ballooned | receivable/unbilled growth vs sales; growth vs parent and peers; delayed results; thin free float |
| Gitanjali Gems' revenue and 'standard' loans (`case_study:hidden-trap-gitanjali-receivables`) | large reported revenue and profits, a big branded jewellery network, loans serviced and classified 'standard' until Dec 2017, 30+ lending banks | receivables were concentrated in group companies (~33% of total receivables) and trade was financed by fraudulent PNB letters of undertaking with ~360-day credit vs a 90-day norm | related-party share of receivables; credit period vs regulation/industry; SMA-2 history; promoter stake trend; number of lenders |
| Cox & Kings' 250-year brand and reported profits (`case_study:hidden-trap-cox-and-kings-brand`) | a 250-year-old global travel brand, reported profits, international subsidiaries (Holidaybreak UK) | a business that collects cash in advance showed high receivables, loans/advances and rising debt; foreign subsidiaries' books were forged | does working-capital sign match the business model; CFO vs PAT; who audits subsidiaries; pledge and CP dependence |
